rationale.campaign_length: The structured library identifies 156 direct B32 mission definitions; the additional 15 B61 The Edhardrachon civil-war missions cannot be added to B32's total for a single campaign.
rationale.colonization: The main line concerns conquering and integrating the old imperial territories; distant expansion is not a core colonisation loop.
rationale.complexity: Formation gates, the Trials, Patricians, Dominions, succession war and situational branches coexist.
rationale.dark_story: Cross-regional expulsions of goblins and gnolls, devastation and money obtained from displaced populations are explicit dark elements of the current missions.
rationale.difficulty: The prologue and Trials, followed by construction and conquest across many regions, can greatly extend a campaign; this has not been measured in play.
rationale.diplomacy: The Patrician estate, Dominions, subjects and succession war require management of internal imperial relations.
rationale.early_pressure: Pressure chiefly belongs to Escanni unification and qualification before formation; B32's post-formation strength has not been playtested.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: The Trials, Dragonforges and later artificery coexist, although warfare and historical restoration remain more central.
rationale.narrative_density: The ancient empire's rise and fall, restoration Trials, revived Legions, succession crisis and the Land of Man objective form an exceptionally long narrative.
rationale.tall_play: Castonath, the ancient walls, citadels, Legion roads, agriculture and industrial facilities impose extensive construction goals.
rationale.trade_economy: Roads, citadels, urban industry and artificer workshops supply an economic dimension; trade is not the sole engine.
rationale.warfare: Warfare and Legions drive the main line from Escanni unification into expansion throughout the ancient empire's regions.

identity.appearance: B32 has no landholding start in 1444; a qualifying Escanni restoration country forms it by passing the Trials of Castan after unlocking the war reward option.
identity.formation_scope: An Adventurer reform, specified previously formed countries or B36 can grant eligibility for the decision. It also requires the Escanni war option, control of Castonath and the North Citadel, the Patrician estate, Human Administration, peace and no previous trial attempt in the ruler's lifetime. For a player, the decision only begins the Trials; the success event changes to B32, moves the capital to 840 and swaps missions. Black Castanor Z34 is excluded; the B61 The Edhardrachon civil-war missions are not direct B32 missions.

description.text:
'Men of Castanor, how can your courage fail you today when the Castanites who founded this Empire walked ten thousand miles to flee slavery and chaos in Bulwar? How can your boldness fail you when two thousands years ago, led by Castan the Progenitor, they chose to fight and die with honour rather than to wait and die by the gnollish demonflame creeping up their fortified hill? To charge downhill, through fire and flame, and to clash with a foe that outnumbered you ten to one, was to be the last act of bravery... but Castellos saw otherwise. And during the Castanite charge, what did Castellos do? He appeared in the form of a Silver Dragon and blew the demonflame back at the gnolls, decisively altering the fate of mankind!

'Men of Castanor, be bold, for your arms will not fail you! Men of Castanor, hold your swords high, for we charge in the name of Castan and the Battle of the Burning Hill! And let our battlecry be heard by the gods, for they will answer with victory!'

description.text: Damenath, Vertesk, Bal Mire, Bal Ouord... The old Castanorian name of those cities and fortresses still today show the extent of the Greater Castan's Empire of the past. We will never forget that Castanor was the first human empire to rule these lands, and it is our sovereign, no, holy duty to take them back into the fold - for only when we rule all of Cannor can the lands be safe.

description.text: Unlike all other cities in Cannor, Castonath was modelled after the dwarven holds of the Serpentspine. And like the greatest dwarven holds, it seems like rather than a city, an entire country was concentrated inside huge walls. All peoples of Escann is represented here, and no merchant can transport goods across Escann without making a stop at the sprawling markets of the City of Stone. For to trade with Escann is to trade with Castonath.

description.text: Castanor's early successes at establishing itself as a great, lasting power was largely due to one dwarf: Balgar the Builder. His unparalleled mastery of architecture allowed for the construction for great works unseen in Cannor, from the legendary Dragonforge that armed the Castanorian Legions, to the White Walls that protected the fledgling empire from monstrous threats, to the famous citadels now scattered across Cannor.

description.text: The Castanorian Legions was the source of Castanor's power, and once marched across Cannor, Bulwar and the Salahad to ensure the empire's power. While the days of antiquity are long gone, we can reform our army structure to follow the old ways, and create an army truly fit for an empire.

description.text:
'Zaamalot the Black flew under the cover of night, burning Castonath to ash. All I could see were corpses and houses set ablaze, and in the flickers of flame I saw that even the white stone of the city had turned black under the Black Dragon's fiery breath. And then came down the sky what looked like a lighting, followed by a deafening but oddly musical roar of thunder. The Silver Dragon of Castanor, the legendary Avatar of Castellos, who helped Castan I at Burning Hill, was coming to our help again - and began to fight with Zaamalot.

'I knelt before the glistening silhouette instinctively, amazed at the creature's might and beauty. For once, the sight of dragonfire filled me with hope, and the flames reflected on his scales, shining so brightly that it seemed dawn had come for a moment. Two years after the end of the Dragonwake, I still feel blessed by this memory. All of our people should feel blessed that twice in history, Castellos himself appeared in the form of the Silver Dragon to save Castanor from a horrible end.'

-Autobiography of Castan XXXVII the Rebuilder

description.text:
It truly is a pity that of all the artifacts recovered by the adventurers after the Greentide, the old silver crown of Castanor is still missing. Hence, when Castanor was rebuilt from its ashes, it was clear to all that the new Castan lacked a fitting crown. From today on, this will not be the case.

Out of silver and mithril, in one year of work, our best smiths forged a huge majestic crown. At the base, shining brightly, is a circlet sculpted to depict the White Walls. Surmounting each tower of the circlet are statues of the gods of the Cannorian Pantheon, encrusted with innumerable jewels. At the center, linked to the interior of the wall by bands of metal, lies an astonishingly accurate representation of Trialmount, topped with a huge diamond!

But that is not all, as there are actually two different parts in this masterpiece! Our smiths forged a splendid miniature dragon, and the most talented enchanter of our realm created an invisible magic link between the two parts, so that the dragon can levitate atop the crown! The mighty Silver Dragon of Castanor deploying its wings around Castan's head as he speaks is truly a sight to behold.

description.text: The Order of the Sapphire Eye was a pre-Greentide knightly order devoted to chivalric virtues and maintaining the peace in Escann, fighting in duels or tourneys known as the 'Trials of Chivalry' as a more peaceful alternative to settle disputes between the Escanni realms. With the rebirth of our kingdom, this order has returned from its near-annihilation to offer us their support in bringing peace back to Escann. Not only does this let our knights train under some of the greatest veterans of the Greentide, it also shows the world the virtue and validity of our claims!

description.text: After the War of the Sorcerer-King, Castanor was broken into disparate realms, some of the greatest of which were the Kingdom of Cast and the Kingdom of Anor. Eventually, these were united under one kingdom - Castellyr, the rightful successor to Castanor. We are the obvious inheritors of this legacy, having accomplished the same.

description.text: Our ambition to bring peace once again to Escann are respected even by our enemies, and even more by our defeated enemies who are often surprised by being integrated as countrymen rather than subjugated as enemies. This makes recruiting local collaborators and solidifying our control over new lands much easier.

description.text: Many of our fellow Escanni fled west as refugees during the Greentide and are now returning to those lands we have pacified. Many have also returned to those lands claimed by the adventurer kingdoms. This makes assimilating the adventurer much easier, as we can simply surround them with native neighbors and let basic socialization do the work.

description.text: With the return of stable government to Escann, chivalry has made a comeback. Though not as idealistic as it was before the Greentide, our chivalric traditions are still enough to motivate our soldiers to act with honor and seek glory.

description.text: The restoration of old Escanni traditions has also seen the resurrection of tourneys, as well as the resolving of disputes between parties through them. Not only does this make escalating to direct conflict socially unacceptable among our nobles, it also provides excellent entertainment for our people and suitable intimidation for would-be rebels.

description.text: Escann was a rich land before the orcs invaded, and we shall make it rich again! We shall sponsor a program of national rejuvenation with the goal of restoring our cities to their former glory.

description.text: The Kingdom of Adenica was the birthplace of the common ideals of "knights" and chivalry. When Adenica fell during the Greentide, that shining beacon of honour and chivalry was lost. With Adenica reforged again, we will rise to meet the ideals of our forefather and shine once more. With righteous hearts, our knights will reclaim their former glory as they ride against injustice.

description.text: Adean is the first-born son of Castellos, and the god of honour, justice and chivalry. When our kingdom was founded, and now refounded, our people embraced these ideals in their entirety. To this end, every man, woman, and child holds this pledge in their hearts: "We are the spear of Adean and all he stands for. No matter what evil we face, we shall not falter."

description.text: There is no doubt in our minds that Corin deserved her ascent to godhood for her valiant sacrifice ending the Greentide. Yet this attempted usurpation of the Regent Court shows that perhaps it was truly Agrados reborn, not Corin ascendant, that has declared war upon the gods. The Corinites do not pledge themselves to Corin and her beliefs, but to Agrados. This vile heresy and desecration of both Corin's name and the Regent Court as a whole cannot be tolerated. We must be the spear of Adean once more.

description.text: When Castanor fell, Adenica fought for its sovereignty against the other successor states. It fought to the last as the Greentide brought ruin to Escann. Even when struck down, its spirit continued to fight. And, through fire, blood and steel, Adenica was reforged. Adenners have never feared fighting for what was right and they are ready and willing to continue that fight once more.

description.text: In Adenica, we pride ourselves on our high standards of honourable conduct. It is a core element of our culture and society, second only to our faith. This high level of honour and respect has led to a vastly lower level of corruption, blackmail and abuse of power within our bureaucracy.

This high level of honour and respect has led to a vastly lower level of corruption, blackmail and abuse of power within our bureaucracy.

description.text: To rule in Adenica, you must prove yourself worthy of rule. To do this, one must obtain knighthood before ascending to the throne. This has been a long standing tradition within our kingdom, and has proven profoundly useful. Our Knight-Kings are known throughout the world for their chivalrous and honourable conduct, and are role models to many rulers and heir-apparents. This reputation has left us in good standing within the global community.

description.text: Our proximity to both the Empire of Anbennar and the reborn realms of Escann have provided us a unique opportunity. We are able to draw on the regulations and innovations of the Western Cannorians, and the military expertise from the Escanni realms. We can leverage this advantage to stay head of the curve, and ensure our ability to protect those in need.

description.text:
The Gleaming Blade was a greatsword used during the Dragonwake by Elecast Dragonsbane to slay the dragon Alos the Copper. While the blade is known for its sharp vorpal quality, it is most famous for the fact that, once drawn, it shines a light that is capable of blinding those who stare too close - this blinding nature of the blade has been used since time immemorial to determine the worthiness of the Blademarcher kings.

During the Decade of Masks it was discovered that the Gleaming Blade was none other than Calindal, a precursor spellblade named after and forged by the mythological elf-smith Calindal.

description.text: The Order of the Bladestewards was a monastic order dedicated to protecting (Calindal, the Gleaming Blade) and ensuring that only the worthy may wield it and rule the Blademarches. Most members of the Blade Stewards are volunteers taken in by the Order, whether it be of unfortunate circumstance or simply a warrior looking for a higher cause. However, a small number of the Blade Stewards are known as Blind Masters, who are comprised of individuals who fail the test of the Gleaming Blade.

description.text:
A famous poem by Lord Wooley during the Fifth Blackpowder War, which details the last charge of the Blademarcher cavalry against a legion of mechanical soldiers:

"the last of the bright hussars came,
with burning hearts and gleaming blade,
onwards to mechanim death: fusillade,
come powder's end: none remained."

-Lord Wooley (1853)

description.text: The symbol of our kingdom and centerpiece of the royal courtyard, the Scoghtrín is a solid black tree grown from a Cursewood sapling first planted in Escin to represent the unity between the elves and men of the eastern Vale. The magics of the tree helped to lessen the effects of the curses that have long plagued this land, and allowed our kingdom to thrive where others have faltered. Though the original may have been destroyed in the Greentide, its legacy lives on in all of us as our banner flies once more over the cities of the Forlorn Vale.

description.text: We have unified the Vale and more beyond, by the union of Elvish Instruction, Human Ingenuity, Half-Elven diplomacy and all those others who have a place in Farranean, we have built an army that surpasses what came before. The old separate armies of Ibevar and Farranean had their own strengths, but now they have come together in one spirit and shall not let the years forsake what unity between us all has brought. Just as there is the unity of spirit, so too comes the unity of technique. Bladedancing, War Magic and the Thunder of Cannons roar as one great cacophony on the fields where battle is drawn when our enemies face the Farrani Army.

description.text: The Orda Aldresia once guarded the Vale and the Empire both against the encroachment of the Corvurian realm, and then when the Greentide came were one of the first refuges for those fleeing the destruction that was wrought upon the continent. Their time is now over, their authority sublimated to that of the Farrani Crown. But this is not a tragic circumstance, for they continue as an order within our realm and their temporal authority ends only because the old promise of Aldresia and the oaths all knight gave stands fulfilled. They have new oaths now, to the Monarchs of Farranean and to the people of the Vale and Escann where once they served the Empire of Anbennar at their own peril. They split on the issue of Escann, but now Escann has mended them in full with our boundless patience.

description.text: The Scogtrin stands now, reflecting the Sun and shining dimly even at night. It stands as a symbol of the nation that can be felt at any time. Across the realm even when it should be impossible, people always feel they can just about see the faint outline of this receptacle of the nation’s hopes and dreams. Such a thing is clearly the work of magic, but it cares little for ostentatious displays of might compared to just bringing all the people together with this shared experience.

description.text: The symbol of our kingdom and centerpiece of the royal courtyard, the Scoghtrín is a solid black tree grown from a Cursewood sapling first planted in Escin to represent the unity between the elves and men of the eastern Vale. The magics of the tree helped to lessen the effects of the curses that have long plagued this land, and allowed our kingdom to thrive where others have faltered. Though the original may have been destroyed in the Greentide, its legacy lives on in all of us as our banner flies once more over the cities of the Forlorn Vale.

description.text: Farraneán has always been a diverse land, a kingdom where elves and men thrived alongside each other as equals and compatriots, forging our unique culture and strategies. From our human roots we take chivalry and horsemanship, our knights charging into battle without fear or worry. From our elven roots we take their skill with the bow, archers supporting the horseman's charge from afar with excellent precision. It is through this fusion of strengths and tactics that Farraneán has survived throughout the centuries, and it will allow us to stand on our own for many more.

description.text: Our kingdom very well may have fallen completely within a few short decades if not for the timely arrival of Lady Aldresia and her noble crusaders. Their actions saved the kingdom and our people, vanquishing the ravenous dead that tormented us. In return for their service and bravery, it has been a long standing tradition for Farrani nobles to send their younger children to join their order, training themselves to defend the weak while also acting as our emissaries, spreading goodwill throughout the courts of Anbennar and ensuring the name of Farraneán is respected and trusted across Cannor.

description.text:
Twice Farraneán has faced catastrophe, and twice we have risen back from sure ruination. Even the destruction of the venerable Scoghtrín was, though incredibly tragic, but a minor setback for us, as her young child now stands proud in the courtyard of Arca Farran, the royal palace. The Caseáns once again guard our villages and townships, while in the woods our men and women work hard to supply timber to the Whistlevale.

The Forlorn Vale has long been a place few tread, fearful of curses and shadowy creatures. But to us, she is home, our cradle and hearth, where we may prosper in harmony. For so long as the Scoghtrín blooms, Farraneán shall blossom.

description.text: The old god of war Agrados was known for his ferocious rage and unyielding blows against his enemies, but Corin saw differently. She saw equal merit in using her powers not only to strike at her foes, but to use them to protect her faithful just the same - no such event can be compared to the Battle of Castonath when Corin raised her shield to defend Lothane Bluetusk from a killing blow by Korgus Dookanson himself, knowing that it would leave her exposed to Korgus' off-hand attack. Accepting her purpose, she used this moment of defense to return the favour and slew Korgus at the cost of her life, ending the Greentide once and for all.

description.text: Corin. Lothane Bluetusk. Dominic of Gallowspeak. Eledas Silurion. All of these names and a dozen more of Corin's Circle have become household names across all of Cannor. We as their successors have big shoes to fill, but their heroism and legacy will never leave us.

description.text: Unlike others, we can claim no exalted lineage nor storied ancestry. We are merely honest men and women from a dozen races and cultures who came together because we believed in something and someone- Corin. Let us promote a new order based on ideals, not origins!

description.text:
"For goodness without action means nothing,

And from nothing, the roots of evil will fester,

For our shields protect, and our swords strike true,

And evil purged means a world saved."

-Corinite Creed

description.text: As more and more people were converted to the Corinite faith, more and more people felt the zeal that her will must be spread across all. This ever-growing group were known as the Corinite Crusaders, and warred across Cannor and even Anbennar itself hoping to bring justice to world.

description.text: When the old Corintar was disbanded and the affairs of the state were under control of the Corinite Crusaders, a new splinter group consisting of moderate Corinites formed a semi-secret society called the New Corintar. These members worked all across the world to secretly ensure that Corin's ideals of freedom, justice and good of man were upheld even beyond the borders of the Corintari state.

description.text:
During the Dragonwake, the Marrodic tribe fled south alongside their Rohibonic and Wexonard brethren to escape the wrath of Godrac the Invader, but the Gawedi Warlord did not relent. But when the Three Tribes were caught at Bal Hyl, alongside allies of convenience in the Damerian garrison of the citadel, they made a last stand. The ensuing victory pushed the Gawedi forces back, and the Damerian offered them land as a reward, and while the Wexonards accepted, the great king Marr had different plans in mind. He directed his people east, through the Korbarid kingdom to the lands of Castanor, recently ruined by the fury of dragons. The Korbarids mocked his plan, but the king was unwavering, and to those who doubted, he said:

“A tree felled by lightning shan't be struck twice!”

This phrase became the embodiment of the Marrodic spirit: a people so bold they seek refuge from the storm within its own eye. Be it during catastrophes or in battle, the Marrodics are steadfast and unwavering, just as King Marr was.

description.text:
Long ago, the hold of Ânumdihr was abandoned, severed from the Serpentspine as the tunnels were destroyed to hold off the monsters lurking in the deep. When the Marrodics reached the hold in 492, they found an empty ruin suitable for their people to settle and rebuild.
So began a long reconstruction effort in which the Marrodics rebuilt the hold; this process cost an astronomical amount of gold, mostly to handsomely reward the dwarven artisans Ulric III ‘the Great’ hired to finish the project. It was an arduous process, but in 549 they managed to fully rebuild the first level, the royal court moving into it soon after. While most remained within the Vale to work mainly as farmers and shepherds, Ânumdihr grew into the city of the Marrvale.

Its halls and homes were adjusted for human size, its walls adorned with tapestries and engraving of Alenic make, and the forges produced vast quantities of longswords and chainmail. No longer was this Ânumdihr, this was Marrhold, and the Marrodics were the Lords of the Vale.

name.text: The Hold of the Griffon King
name.text_en: The Hold of the Griffon King

description.text:
Legend has it that as the Marrodics settled the Marrvale and its great, though dilapidated and abandoned Dwarven hold, they were set upon by terrifying winged creatures that would descend from the mountains. With many either dying or being wounded by these attacks, King Marr sent his son, Ulric, to face these monsters. It is said Prince Ulric climbed high into the Serpentspine Mountains, reaching the nest of the griffons at the top. There, he battled them for many hours, eventually vanquishing the threat to his people. Once he had, however, he chose to spare their eggs, taking many with him on his descent.

In time, these griffons would grow into mighty steeds granted to King Marr’s finest warriors, with Ulric as the first Griffon Rider atop his steed, ‘Thundersteed’. Over the centuries, the Griffon Knights would come to dominate Marrodic society, the position given only to the highest ranking nobles, with the breeding and rearing of the steeds being a highly protected and regulated affair.

While some call our reliance on them foolish, citing our rigid social structure and low number of these elite troops, there is a reason why even after the Dragonwake, even the mightiest lords of Cannor dread the sight of something moving in the skies.

description.text:
Aerial jousting is one of the pillars of a Griffon-Knight’s training. This tradition dates back to the year 503, when Ulric I chose the first Griffon-Knights. Since then the practice has evolved many times, first as a purely military drill, then as a noble tournament, but it was only in 1386 where both practices were officially conjoined.

Two different jousts are hosted each year in different locations and times.
One is the traditional course of training, occurring in winter deep within the mountains above Marrhold, with scant few onlookers having ever caught a glimpse of this event. This training is reputed to be most arduous, carried out in extreme wind and snow.
The second is a grand summer festival held in Griffonsgate, open to any citizen of Marrhold, in which Griffon-Knights show off in magnificent parade attire with long white cloaks floating in the wind. This event is famed for being the only opportunity to see so many griffons in the same place and for the aerial choreographies of renowned Griffon-Knights.

description.text:
Unlike his grandfather, Gryf ‘the Young’ was a very skilled griffon rider gifted with a most astute mind. Indeed, most say that it was thanks to his efforts that Marrhold managed to obtain a secure position in Escann following the breaking of the Greentide and Korgus’ death. This was only amplified by his decision to defy his orders and fight when he sallied forth to help Corin during the battle of Castonath and ended up being one of the decisive factors as a skilled fighter, talented commander, and inspiring presence.

When he inherited the throne, Gryf VIII ‘the Young’ decided to revitalize the Griffon-Knights by allowing the lower nobility and even distinguished commoners to obtain a griffon. While this was a controversial measure, its success led to a renaissance of the chivalric values that had been dwindling during the first half of the 15th century, and the newly reformed Griffon-Knights ended up at the forefront of the reclamation of Escann.

description.text:
To ensure the safety of the kingdom, generation after generation of kings fortified the Marrvale, resulting in a sturdy system of fortifications able to resist and repel most invaders. In the event of a prolonged siege, secret passes allow us to keep them supplied and manned. If a fort were to fall, the enemy would be allowed deeper in the multi-layered fortification system and their supplies harassed using the secret passages; ultimately, a deathly trap would close behind the enemies as any fort taken would be retaken by the Marrodics, isolating the enemies in a sea of hostile forts and trapped passages.
This formation of forts was nicknamed “The Death Ring of Marrvale” by an enemy general that had its army cut in two and decimated by the formation.

As such, the Marrhold was unbroken. None managed to reach it for centuries; neither Nichmer, Dookanson, and though Marrhold submitted to Camir, not even he tried to besiege the hold, a source of great pride for the Marrodics.

description.text:
What made the Griffon-Knights unique was their ability to meld both mobility and speed, and the knights primarily focused on shock and awe tactics. But, with the rise of artificers, warfare changed drastically, slowly rendering the Griffon-Knights less efficient and relevant. King Ulric XVII Marr could not bear to see what many believe to be Marrhold’s strength be relegated to a simple exotic pet; as such, he invested greatly in our local artificers, commissioning them to develop weapons enabling the Griffon-Knights to attack while remaining airborne, whatever the conditions. The artificers worked quickly,both draining the treasury of the kingdom and creating what was required of them.
As such, in 1757, the new evolution of the Griffon-Knights was created, a high-flying formation dropping weighted explosives from the heavens. Known as the Griffon Bombardier Squadron, they quickly replaced the traditional Griffon-Knights. The Bombardier Squadron were devastatingly effective, but to be deployed properly, they had to be able to resupply with ammunition and not be completely exposed to incoming fire, for griffons remained vulnerable to shot and shell during both the dive and during the climb after.

Known as the Griffon Bombardier Squadron, they quickly replaced the traditional Griffon-Knights. The Bombardier Squadron were devastatingly effective, but to be deployed properly, they had to be able to resupply with ammunition and not be completely exposed to incoming fire, for griffons remained vulnerable to shot and shell during both the dive and during the climb after.

player_overview.avoid_if: Players wanting to start directly as B32 in 1444, unwilling to meet formation and trial gates, or averse to explicit population-expulsion narratives.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Qualify for the Trials through an eligible Escanni predecessor; after formation restore Legions, cities and roads while managing Patricians and frontier Dominions, then face succession crises, cross-regional expansion and imperial cultural projects.
player_overview.overview: Castanor is not a 1444 starting country. Reclaim Castonath with an eligible Escanni state, gain restoration eligibility and pass the Trials before actually becoming B32. Restore the ancient Legions, citadels and roads, manage Patricians and Dominions, expand into the old imperial territories and establish a new empire calling itself the Land of Man. Explicit expulsions of goblins and gnolls are the dark side of this long restoration epic.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy an Escanni prologue, ancient imperial history, exceptionally long Legion conquests, citadel building and political succession crises.
signature_features: The formation decision starts the Trials of Castan; only the success event changes Tag, moves the capital and switches to imperial missions.
156 direct B32 missions span ancient Legions, citadels and roads, Dominions, succession war and distant conquests.
Extensive public construction and historical exploration coexist with forced expulsions of goblins and gnolls.
player_overview.tagline: Pass the Trials to become the next Castan and rebuild Escann's ruins into a Legion empire spanning Cannor.

reasons: The Trials give imperial restoration a concrete personal and political gate.
Legions, ancient cities, roads and Dominions create a distinctive military-administrative construction loop.
156 direct B32 missions provide an exceptionally long historical and expansionist main line.
warnings: Formation eligibility must first be gained through a qualifying Escanni predecessor.
The mission count and construction gates are enormous; older-version players questioned whether completion before 1821 was possible.
The narrative explicitly includes goblin and gnoll expulsions and revenue obtained from displaced populations.

phase_scores.phase: Cross-regional expulsions of goblins and gnolls

positive_indicators: The mission narrative opposes gnoll slavery.
Supporting long-term cooperation between dwarves and humans.
Restoring citadels, roads, agriculture and industrial facilities.
values.rationale: War, forming an empire, monarchy and ordinary cultural integration do not automatically lower the score. The current missions explicitly change goblin and gnoll provinces' religion and culture, add 50 devastation and remove their minorities; localisation calls this expulsion and awards money for expelled populations. This is cross-regional institutional deprivation. Anti-slavery language, dwarf–human cooperation, agriculture and urban projects benefit the public, but do not cancel the expulsion policies.
red_flags: Mission effects forcibly change goblin and gnoll provinces' religion and culture and add 50 devastation.
Relevant minorities are removed, the localisation explicitly calls it expulsion, and treasury revenue is awarded for the expelled population.
A human-centred imperial identity denies other sapient peoples full political personhood.
